title: Model acquisition stress-test & regional readiness playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: produce an operational playbook and measurable probe suite that stress-tests our model sourcing and fallback choices across regions. Background: customers in EU/APAC have reported intermittent degradations when upstream providers change quantization or capacity. We need a repeatable way to detect: (A) model-quality regressions vs. our baseline prompts, (B) regional availability shocks (throttled/removed variants), and (C) economic breakpoints that should trigger procurement/rollout actions. Outcome: an artifact that ties signals (latency, error-rate, eval-quality delta, cost-per-1000-tokens) to prescribed runbooks and procurement thresholds so Sales/SRE/Procurement can act without ad-hoc analysis.
acceptance_criteria: A probe harness that runs 4 synthetic workloads (short-chat, RAG-LLM, embeddings-batch, long-context completion) across 3 regions weekly
Dashboards showing delta from baseline for latency, p95, error-rate, and quality (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity) with alert thresholds defined
A written playbook with decision tree: when to trigger Reserved Capacity bid, when to fallback to quantized variant, and when to engage supplier (procurement)
Automated weekly report emailed to SRE/Product/Procurement with recommended actions and confidence score
tasks: Draft probe spec and seed workload corpus (owner: Liam) - include 50 canonical prompts per workload
Implement probe runner in infra (owner: ENG - assign ENG-?? ticket) - containerized, parallelized per-region
Create dashboard panels in Console (owner: Observability team) - latency, quality-drift, cost
Define procurement threshold matrix (owner: PM) - cost delta, outage duration, quality drop
Author playbook doc in Confluence with decision tree and escalation contacts
Run initial two-week sweep across EU-West, US-East, APAC-SG and collect results
Post-mortem & refine probe parameters based on false-positive rate
updates: 2026-02-20 - Asha Patel: Scoped initiative after 3 customer reports of regression in EU. Framed output as 'probe + playbook + dashboard' to bridge Product/SRE/Procurement.
2026-02-25 - Liam O'Connor: Completed seed workload corpus (50 prompts/workload). Uploaded CSVs to Drive and added README describing metric mapping.
2026-03-02 - ENG: PoC probe runner PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/1839). Runner supports parallel per-region sampling and stores raw token-level traces.
2026-03-04 - Observability: Prototype dashboard panels created; need labels and model_variant filter. Requesting model metadata from Model-Onboarding (ENG-2201).

2026-03-07 - PM review (Maya): Suggested adding a confidence decay window to avoid reacting to single-day anomalies. Decision: require 3-day sustained delta or 24hr severe outage to trigger immediate escalation.

2026-03-09 - Initial sweep (EU-West, US-East, APAC-SG) completed. Findings: quantized-8bit variant of 'open-flare-7B' shows 12% increase in latency p95 in APAC-SG and a 6-point drop in semantic-similarity for RAG workload. Artifact uploaded to Drive.
2026-03-10 - Meeting notes: Decided to tag model variants with 'procurement-risk' when quality-delta > 5% AND sustained for >72h. Action: Observability to create alert and weekly digest (ENG-2755).
decisions: Use a blended quality metric (semantic-similarity + task-specific QA) rather than single metric to lower false positives
Require sustained signal (>=72 hours) for non-severe regressions before procurement escalation
Automate fallback to a pinned model-variant in the same region for up to 48 hours while procurement engages for replacement/reserve capacity
Expose a procurement-ready CSV export with ranked candidate substitutes and estimated cost delta
risks: False positives from transient upstream throttles leading to unnecessary procurement churn
Probe workload not representative of all customers — risk of underfitting signals to niche verticals
Cost of continuous probes (tokens) vs marginal value — need to cap sampling budget
Regional quota/shaping differences may bias comparisons if not normalized
